modules.module_title: Prepare and align the liner and medium (fluting) paper reels

pcs.pc_description: identify the correct type, size, and GSM of liner and fluting paper reels as per the job order or production plan
use mechanical or hydraulic reel handling equipment to safely lift and load the paper reels onto the unwind stand
check for physical defects in the paper reels such as tears, creases, or moisture patches before loading
align the liner and medium paper accurately over the guide rollers and feed pathways to ensure smooth entry into the single facer unit
adjust reel brakers and tension controls to maintain consistent web tension during unwinding and feeding
ensure correct paper orientation and threading to match flute direction and bonding alignment
verify that paper reels are locked and secured properly to avoid misfeed or displacement during operation
record reel usage details (paper type, roll number, and weight) in the shift log or production register
interpret job sheet or production schedule to identify required board grade, flute type, and glue specifications for the production run
set the flute roll and preheater temperature based on the paper GSM, moisture content, and bonding requirements
adjust nip roller and pressure roll settings to ensure proper contact between the flute and liner without crushing the board
calibrate the glue applicator roller to control glue film thickness and uniform spread across the fluting tips
verify the adhesive viscosity and glue temperature, and adjust the application settings accordingly
confirm alignment and engagement of pressure roll and glue roll as per the defined flute profile (A, B, C, etc.)
test run the machine in idle mode (without paper) to verify parameter settings and detect abnormal noise, vibrations, or leakage
record all setup parameters and settings in the machine logbook for traceability and future reference

modules.module_title: Conduct pre-start machine inspection and dry run

pcs.pc_description: inspect the single facer machine components including rollers, belts, glue pans, and steam pipes for any visible wear, damage, or obstructions
ensure all safety guards, interlocks, and emergency stop buttons are functional and accessible before initiating machine operations
verify the readiness of utility systems such as steam supply, glue circulation, and air pressure to ensure they are within operational range
check the alignment of loaded paper reels and proper threading over guide rollers to prevent feeding issues during start-up
conduct a dry run (machine run without paper) to observe roller movement, motor function, adhesive roller rotation, and detect unusual noises or vibrations
report any abnormalities or deviations identified during inspection or dry run to the supervisor or maintenance team for immediate corrective action

modules.module_title: Operate the single facer machine during live production

pcs.pc_description: ensure continuous and smooth feeding of fluting and liner paper into the single facer unit without reel displacement or paper misalignment
operate the machine at the prescribed speed and pressure, maintaining optimal flute formation and consistent bonding quality
regulate adhesive flow and roller engagement to ensure even glue application on fluted tips during production
monitor flute profile and bonding visually and physically at intervals to confirm proper adhesion and avoid delamination
detect signs of improper bonding, glue skips, or liner shifting, and make immediate adjustments or alert the supervisor
maintain coordination with adhesive preparation and corrugation control teams to adjust inputs based on machine response or job changeovers

modules.module_title: Monitor and control key process parameters

pcs.pc_description: monitor steam pressure and flute roll temperature to ensure proper heat transfer for effective corrugation of medium paper
adjust machine speed based on paper type, moisture content, and bonding behavior to ensure consistent flute formation
observe glue application consistency and regulate adhesive flow to avoid over-gluing, skips, or uneven bonding
check nip pressure settings regularly to ensure sufficient contact between the liner and fluted paper without crushing
use control panel indicators or gauges to track real-time process values and make timely adjustments as required
record key process parameters (e.g., temperature, pressure, speed) in the production log at defined intervals
identify unusual process fluctuations such as glue foaming, temperature drop, or paper warp and report immediately
ensure that all monitored parameters align with job card specifications and quality standards throughout the shift
visually inspect the flute profile for proper shape, height, and uniformity during machine operation
check bonding between liner and fluting using manual methods (e.g., peel test) at periodic intervals to assess adhesion strength
identify common quality defects such as delamination, warping, glue skips, and liner misalignment during the run
monitor paper tracking and ensure that liners and medium are correctly aligned throughout the width of the board
take immediate corrective actions (e.g., adjust glue flow, roller pressure, or paper tension) or inform the supervisor when defects are detected
record quality check observations and corrective actions taken in the in-process quality checklist or production log
